transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-07-09 09:23 UTC | Duration: 46 minutes | Attendees: Alex Chen, Priya Nair, Samir Patel (Redwood); Maya Ito, Daniel Ortiz, Lina Park, Ravi Menon (Pinehaven Labs)

Summary (auto): quick renewal sync; primary ask is to add APAC on-prem pilot and additional 20% monthly capacity; security + procurement blockers noted; next steps around SOW, benchmarks, and network details.

00:00 - Alex Chen: alright good morning everyone, thanks for joining us, uh we're here to walk through the renewal and the APAC on prem pilot ask from Pinehaven. i'm alex chen, AE, i'll run the agenda quickly.
00:12 - Maya Ito: hey alex, thanks. morning from tokyo side. we'll try to keep time, lina from procurement is on the line to cover contract questions.
00:20 - Daniel Ortiz: morning, quick note we have a scheduled maintenance at 2am JST later this week so any heavy testing should avoid that window.

02:10 - Alex Chen: recap — current commitment ends sept, you're set on Dedicated pool with us, used roughly 78% steady-state, spikes to 140% during model training windows, request is twofold: 1) 20% uplift to commitments for next term, 2) run an APAC on-prem pilot for data residency and latency sensitive workloads. correct me if i'm wrong.
02:33 - Maya Ito: that's right, the 20% is to account for feature growth. On-prem pilot is non-negotiable for regulated clients in JP, we need <50ms p50 for short responses.
03:05 - Priya Nair: quick technical read: on-prem pilot we typically provide a private control plane and either a VPC-hosted or customer-managed on-prem package. we need to confirm network egress, KMS choices, and which model variant you want to pin.
03:34 - Ravi Menon: KMS is important — we use an HSM-backed KMS; we need to confirm key custody options, audit trails, and encryption-in-transit standards. we logged SOC2 and ISO requests already.

05:01 - Alex Chen: noted, we'll include KMS/HSM options. pricing impact: on-prem pilots carry a setup fee plus a slightly higher unit cost for dedicated private nodes until we stabilize. i'll follow up with a SOW that separates hosted vs on-prem cost lines.
05:27 - Lina Park: procurement note — we need traffic egress estimates, and an estimate of storage for KV cache if it persists on-prem, also SLAs for pilot.
05:46 - Samir Patel: for the pilot we usually offer a 6-week window: week 1-2 integration, 3-4 load/baseline, 5-6 tuning and handover. SLA for pilot is different from GA commitments, but we can commit to response latencies and runbooks.

08:10 - Daniel Ortiz: curious about the failure modes and fallback — if on-prem capacity hits limits, can traffic route to hosted in APAC or US? we need automatic failover with consistent model variants.
08:36 - Priya Nair: yes, our smart routing supports fallbacks to hosted or to a cold spare. there is model variant compatibility to verify — if you pin a heavily quantized variant on-prem, fallback might need a compatible hosted variant to avoid quality regressions.
09:05 - Maya Ito: quality drift is a concern; we do not want users to see different hallucination rates between on-prem and hosted. do you have evaluation tooling?
09:21 - Alex Chen: Redwood Optimize includes eval hooks; we can run side-by-side diff on our eval sets. we'll share initial eval templates and recommend acceptance criteria.

11:00 - Lina Park: procurement timeline — we need the final SOW by 2026-07-20 to make the board cycle for an August contract sign. can you hit that?
11:18 - Alex Chen: yes we'll aim for earlier; i'll send a draft SOW by 2026-07-14 and then address comments.

13:05 - Maya Ito: on the benchmarking, for latency tests we'll provide a sample of typical prompts — mostly short token summaries, sometimes 4-6 sentence answers. can you commit to running throughput tests with our samples?
13:29 - Priya Nair: yes, we'll run a 1k-request baseline with your prompts and measure p50/p90/p99, token cost, and concurrency effects. please note results will vary by quantization and runtime kernel choices.

15:02 - Daniel Ortiz: network — we use private peering and strict egress rules, we need details for firewall rules, allowed IP ranges, and TLS fingerprinting. who owns the peering setup?
15:20 - Alex Chen: typically the customer provisions a peering and we provide the allowed IPs and ports. for on-prem, if you'd prefer, we can schedule our infra team to coordinate the peering setup with your network ops.
15:48 - Daniel Ortiz: okay we'll get the network owners in thread; i'll share constraints by monday.

18:10 - Ravi Menon: security artifacts — we need an RSA-signed SOC2 attestation, encryption key flow diagrams, and audit log schema for retention. is that standard?
18:28 - Samir Patel: yes, we can share SOC2 summary and an audit log export sample. the on-prem option allows you to keep logs locally if needed, and we support integrating with your SIEM.

20:05 - Maya Ito: about pricing — the hosted cost per token is acceptable, but on-prem gives us the sovereignty we need. what kind of discounting or commitment incentives are there for a 12 month renewal with the 20% uplift?
20:23 - Alex Chen: we can propose a tiered commitment: 12 months with 20% uplift gets a 7% blended discount vs list for hosted token consumption; on-prem pilot billed separately as one-off setup plus discounted private node hours during pilot. i'll reflect numbers in the SOW.

23:00 - Lina Park: procurement asks to see a sample contract amendment showing the uplift and billing cadence. also need payment terms, and any limits on data egress costs.
23:22 - Alex Chen: understood — we'll include an amendment template and specify egress assumptions. we try to be transparent on unit economics.

25:10 - Priya Nair: technical note — if Pinehaven wants p50 <50ms for short responses, that typically means local inference or very close edge. our APAC on-prem pilot should be able to hit that if the model size and batch configs are tuned; we'll share suggested quantization and batching profiles.
25:43 - Maya Ito: our core responses are short, but we also have long-form summarization internally — that can run hosted during non-regulated flows.

28:05 - Daniel Ortiz: question about KV cache: if we persist KV cache on-prem between bursts, we need to know disk footprint and expected eviction patterns. what's typical?
28:24 - Priya Nair: depends on avg seq lengths; for your workload we'd estimate 10-50GB for persistent KV per 8 GPUs. we'll run numbers during the baseline.

30:00 - Maya Ito: are there any known gotchas when moving from hosted to private nodes regarding tokenization differences or tokenizer versions? we've seen subtle differences before with other vendors.
30:21 - Priya Nair: good point — tokenizer versions can cause subtle log-prob shifts. we track tokenizer mappings in our model catalog and will lock versions in the SOW. we'll also run diff tests.

32:40 - Lina Park: legal question — indemnity and data residency clauses, we probably need to add an addendum for JP clients for the pilot; can you share a sample addendum?
32:52 - Alex Chen: yes, we'll pull a sample addendum that has been used for other APAC pilots (redacted). i'll coordinate with legal and attach it to the SOW.

35:10 - Daniel Ortiz: operational handover — after pilot completion, what's the handoff for runbooks and on-call? do we get a dedicated SE for the first month?
35:27 - Samir Patel: we provide dedicated SE engagement during integration and a handover document. first-month escalation is included for pilots, and optional extended on-call can be added to the support package.

37:00 - Maya Ito: timeline recap — we want pilot to start tentative 2026-08-02 if SOW signed in late July. is that feasible?
37:12 - Priya Nair: tight but doable. we need network details and initial access by 2026-07-22 to hit that start date.
37:26 - Daniel Ortiz: noted. will try to prioritize.

39:45 - Alex Chen: let's do a quick recap and owners — i'll send SOW draft by 2026-07-14. Priya will run benchmark and share by 2026-07-16. Daniel will share network constraints by 2026-07-12. Ravi to confirm security artifacts by 2026-07-15. procurement (Lina) to confirm board timeline and sign-off window.
40:15 - Lina Park: yep, sign-off target is end of July so we can onboard in August.

42:00 - Maya Ito: any other risks we haven't covered? model parity during fallback still concerns me.
42:12 - Priya Nair: we'll include acceptance criteria with concrete eval metrics and a rollback/fallback plan.

44:05 - Alex Chen: ok thanks everyone. i'll follow up with a calendar invite for the benchmark kickoff and attach SOW draft when available.
44:17 - Maya Ito: thanks all. bye.
44:25 - meeting ends
notes: Customer emphasized <50ms p50 requirement for APAC on-prem short responses
Procurement needs SOW draft and sample amendment for JP clients by 2026-07-14/20
Redwood will run a 1k-request throughput baseline and share results
